On Aug. 17th through the 21st I took a week-long crash course on how to use R for Data Science.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source(file.path(Sys.getenv("QUARTO_PROJECT_DIR", "../.."), "R/theme_isai.R"))
use_isai_defaults()
```

```{r}
#| label: MPG in city vs highway
#| fig-alt: "Scatterplot of city versus highway fuel economy in miles per gallon for cars in the mpg dataset, showing that cars with better city mileage also get better highway mileage."
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)

ggplot(
  data = mpg, 
  mapping = aes(
    x = cty,
    y = hwy
  )
)+ geom_point()


```

This is great, but one thing we learned about is the importance of clear labels using the `labs()` function.

```{r}
#| label: c2
#| fig-alt: "The same city versus highway mileage scatterplot with a smoothed trend line rising from left to right, an axis label on each axis, and the title City vs Highway."
#| echo: true
library(tidyverse)

ggplot(
  data = mpg, 
  mapping = aes(
    x = cty,
    y = hwy
  )
)+ geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth() + 
  labs(
    x = "City Mileage",
    y = "Highway Mileage", 
    title = "City vs Highway"
  )
```
